name: Ocean Coworker Rollout Prep
purpose: Take the V0 local sync GUI (scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs) and raw-token-paste onboarding to a safe, repeatable coworker rollout: replace raw-token-paste with a one-time server-issued invite code redeemed for a scoped token; add default secret-exclusion globs so credentials/keys never sync; give the dry-run a real skipped/sensitive-file review surface before first upload; issue contributor-only scoped tokens (delete already blocked) and verify the scope/clearance gates; harden the token registry from volume-JSON (src/auth.mjs + data/.ocean-bedrock/tokens.json) to a Postgres-backed table (db/004) so multi-replica is possible; package or document the GUI install; and ship a written operator onboarding + revoke/rotate runbook.

canonicalBoundaries.oceanDaemon: Local runtime/body and execution authority. Owns local sessions, events, tools, provider execution, local filesystem/shell/destructive permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanLonghouse: Hive brain / coordination layer per ocean-os/docs/LONGHOUSE.md. Coordinates skills, SOPs, routines, MCP discovery, memory, subagents, quorum/council logic. Does not bypass daemon permissions.
canonicalBoundaries.oceanBedrock: Cloud-box support substrate for shared files, context ingest, ledger/event store, Postgres/R2/Vectorize/KV, MCP-facing infrastructure, and coworker bootstrap. Does not redefine Longhouse.

currentState: Onboarding today is raw-token-paste: scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs renders a password field "Paste token once" and stores the literal bearer in ~/.config/ocean-bedrock/bootstrap.json (mode 0600); requireConfigured() even says "Paste and save your invite/token first" but no invite redemption exists — authenticate() in src/server.mjs (line ~225) only calls findToken(auth, token) against the volume-JSON registry. The token registry is file-based (src/auth.mjs loadAuthFile/addToken/revokeToken over data/.ocean-bedrock/tokens.json), sha256-hashed, 5 roles (readonly/contributor/readwrite/agent/admin) with contributor=read/write/lock (delete already blocked) and CONFIDENTIAL max clearance; server token admin routes GET/POST /api/v1/tokens and DELETE /api/v1/tokens/:id (lines ~1652-1676) all require admin. There is NO Postgres token table — db/ ends at 003_source_adapters.sql — so the registry is single-replica-only. Secret exclusion does NOT exist: DEFAULT_IGNORES in scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs, scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs, and scripts/ocean-bootstrap.mjs only filter build dirs (.git, node_modules, dist...) — there are no globs for .env, *.pem, id_rsa, *.key, credentials, .aws/.ssh. The ingest --dry-run builds a manifest with totals.skipped and per-source skipped counts but never records WHICH files were skipped or flags sensitive matches, so there is no review surface before first upload.

phases.title: Pin canonical boundaries and live source-of-truth
tasks: Re-read CANONICAL BOUNDARY: ocean-daemon = local runtime/body/execution authority; ocean-longhouse = hive brain/coordination layer; ocean-bedrock = cloud-box support substrate. This track touches ONLY Bedrock onboarding/auth/ingest — do not redefine Longhouse or claim Bedrock is the quorum engine.

Confirm the live token model against running code, not stale docs: src/auth.mjs roles (readonly/contributor/readwrite/agent/admin), contributor permissions = read/write/lock with delete already blocked (src/server.mjs ROLE_PERMISSIONS line ~70), CONFIDENTIAL max clearance (ROLE_MAX_CLEARANCE line ~188).
Record that the token registry is currently volume-JSON (data/.ocean-bedrock/tokens.json) and therefore single-replica-only; this is the gap Postgres hardening closes.
Treat 'invite exchange' and 'GUI packaging choice' as open decisions to resolve in-spec, not pre-decided facts; capture any product-naming uncertainty as an open decision.
acceptance: Spec text never claims Bedrock is Longhouse or the quorum engine.
Phase docs state the registry is volume-JSON single-replica today and Postgres is the target.
No raw token, invite secret, or DATABASE_URL value is written into any committed artifact.

phases.title: Verify contributor-only scopes, clearance, and delete-block
tasks: Issue a real contributor token scoped to /coworkers/<name>, /sessions/<name>, /context/ocean-bedrock via POST /api/v1/tokens (admin) or npm run token:create -- --role contributor --scope ...; capture the raw token only over a secure channel.
Confirm requirePathScope (src/server.mjs line ~174) rejects writes outside the granted scopes and requirePermission blocks delete for contributor (ROLE_PERMISSIONS.contributor has no 'delete').
Confirm requireClearance caps the contributor token at CONFIDENTIAL and TOP_SECRET/SECRET-tagged ledger events are not visible (ledgerEventVisibleToPrincipal line ~210).
Document the canonical coworker scope convention in docs/COWORKER-BOOTSTRAP.md security section, replacing the current generic note.
List the 9 historical failed ingest_jobs and 8 registry-only adapters as out-of-scope-for-onboarding so a new coworker is not blocked by them.
acceptance: A contributor token can PUT under /coworkers/<name>/... and is rejected (403) writing to /vault or another coworker's prefix.
DELETE /api/v1/file with the contributor token returns 403 (delete blocked).
A SECRET/TOP_SECRET ledger event is not returned to the contributor token.
docs/COWORKER-BOOTSTRAP.md states the exact scope set issued to coworkers.

phases.title: Default secret-exclusion globs for ingest
tasks: Add a shared DEFAULT_SECRET_PATTERNS list (new module src/ingest-filters.mjs) covering: .env and .env.* , *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, id_rsa/id_dsa/id_ecdsa/id_ed25519 (+ .pub off, private on), *.keystore, credentials, *.tfstate, .npmrc, .pypirc, .netrc, .htpasswd, .aws/, .ssh/, .gnupg/, *.kdbx (KeePass), service-account*.json, *secret*, *credential* (case-insensitive).

Wire DEFAULT_SECRET_PATTERNS into scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs shouldIncludeFile/walk and into the DEFAULT_IGNORES of scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs + scripts/ocean-bootstrap.mjs so the same filter applies in dry-run, GUI sync, and CLI bootstrap.
Classify two outcomes per excluded file: 'noise' (build dirs, already ignored) vs 'sensitive' (matched a secret pattern) so the dry-run can warn loudly on sensitive matches.
Make the secret filter NON-overridable by --all-files / all-files mode (size/extension override is fine; secrets stay excluded unless an explicit, separately-named --include-secrets flag is passed).
Add a unit-style check in scripts/smoke-test.mjs (or a new scripts/check-secret-globs.mjs) asserting a temp dir with .env, id_rsa, secrets.json is fully excluded by default.
acceptance: A folder containing .env, id_rsa, aws-credentials, secret.pem, app.kdbx ingests ZERO of those files by default (dry-run totals show them under skipped/sensitive).
--all-files still excludes the secret set; only the explicit --include-secrets flag changes that.
The check script exits 0 and reports each blocked sensitive file with its matched pattern.
DEFAULT_SECRET_PATTERNS is defined once (src/ingest-filters.mjs) and imported by all three scripts (no copy-paste divergence).

phases.title: Dry-run skipped/sensitive-file review before first upload
tasks: Extend the ingest manifest in scripts/ocean-ingest-local.mjs to record a skippedFiles array per source: { rel, reason: 'size'|'extension'|'ignore'|'sensitive', matchedPattern? }, gated to dry-run or a --report flag to avoid bloating real-run manifests.

Add a --review (or reuse --dry-run) summary block to the JSON output: counts by reason plus the full list of 'sensitive' matches surfaced first, so an operator sees credentials-that-would-have-synced before any upload.

In scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs add a 'Dry-run / Preview' button and /api/preview endpoint that runs ingest with --dry-run and renders changed-file count, skipped-by-reason counts, and a red 'Sensitive files excluded' panel listing matched paths.
Block the GUI 'Sync now' / first real upload behind an explicit 'I reviewed the preview' acknowledgement when any sensitive match was found in the latest preview.
Keep raw file bytes out of the preview payload — surface paths and reasons only, never file contents.
acceptance: npm run ocean:ingest -- --dry-run prints a skippedFiles list with reason and matchedPattern for each sensitive hit.
GET/POST /api/preview in the local app returns changed count + skipped-by-reason counts + sensitive matches and renders the red panel.
When a sensitive match is present, the GUI requires explicit acknowledgement before enabling the first real sync.
Preview output contains paths/reasons only, no file contents.

phases.title: Harden token registry from volume-JSON to Postgres
tasks: Author db/004_auth_tokens.sql creating longhouse.auth_tokens (id TEXT PK, name, hash TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, role TEXT, scopes JSONB/TEXT[], created_at, created_by, expires_at, revoked_at, revoked_by) with an index on hash; keep sha256: hash format identical to src/auth.mjs hashToken so existing tokens stay valid.

Add a Postgres backend to src/auth.mjs behind the SAME function signatures (loadAuthFile/findToken/addToken/revokeToken/publicTokenRecord) — introduce a store abstraction selected by OCEAN_AUTH_STORE (postgres when DATABASE_URL set, else json), preserving sha256 hashing, roles, normalizeScopes, expiry, timing-safe compare.

Write scripts/migrate-tokens-to-postgres.mjs that backfills every record from data/.ocean-bedrock/tokens.json into longhouse.auth_tokens idempotently (ON CONFLICT (hash) DO NOTHING), preserving id/role/scopes/createdAt/revokedAt; require --yes like scripts/migrate.mjs.
Update db/003-style migration list in scripts/migrate.mjs default files to include db/004; keep findToken on a hot path query (indexed hash lookup), not a full table scan.
Update docs/HANDOFF.md to mark the token registry as Postgres-backed and multi-replica-capable once cut over, and note OCEAN_AUTH_STORE env.
acceptance: npm run db:migrate -- --yes db/004_auth_tokens.sql applies cleanly; longhouse.auth_tokens exists with a UNIQUE index on hash.
With OCEAN_AUTH_STORE=postgres, authenticate() resolves a known token via DB and an unknown/revoked token returns 403 (parity with JSON backend).
scripts/migrate-tokens-to-postgres.mjs backfills all current tokens.json rows; re-running is a no-op (row count unchanged).
Token create/revoke via /api/v1/tokens writes to Postgres and is visible after a simulated second-replica read (fresh connection).

phases.title: One-time invite code redeemed for a scoped token
tasks: Design a short-lived single-use invite: admin POST /api/v1/invites { name, role:'contributor', scopes, ttlMinutes } returns an invite CODE (high-entropy, stored sha256-hashed in a new longhouse.auth_invites table in db/004 alongside tokens) with expires_at and consumed_at NULL; the raw scoped token is NOT created until redemption.

Add public-ish POST /api/v1/invites/redeem { code } that, if the invite is unconsumed and unexpired, atomically marks it consumed and mints a contributor token (addToken with the invite's role/scopes), returning the raw token ONCE; reject reuse, expired, or unknown codes.

Replace raw-token-paste in scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs: add a 'Redeem invite' field that POSTs the code to /api/v1/invites/redeem, then stores the returned scoped token in bootstrap.json (mode 0600) — coworker never sees or pastes a long raw token.
Update requireConfigured() messaging and docs so the path is 'paste invite code once' not 'paste token'; keep a fallback raw-token path for admins/agents.
Ensure invite codes and minted tokens are never written to shared manifests or ledger payloads — only token id/name/role/scopes metadata.
acceptance: POST /api/v1/invites (admin) returns an invite code and persists a hashed row; the code is shown once.
POST /api/v1/invites/redeem with a valid code mints a contributor token and returns it once; a second redeem of the same code returns 4xx (single-use).
An expired invite code is rejected with 4xx.
The local app 'Redeem invite' flow stores a working scoped token and never displays the raw token after redemption.
No invite code or raw token appears in any /context manifest or ledger payload.

phases.title: Package/install the GUI and write the operator runbook
tasks: Weigh GUI packaging options and record the decision: (A) documented 'node scripts/ocean-local-app.mjs via npx/npm run ocean:app' with a one-line installer script (lowest effort, recommended for first rollout), (B) Electron/Tauri double-click .app/.exe (higher effort, defer). Default to (A) for this wave and capture (B) as a follow-up.

Create scripts/ocean-install.sh (and a Windows note) that checks Node >=22, clones/pulls the repo or installs a published tarball, runs npm install, and prints the ocean:app command — no token baked in.

Write docs/COWORKER-ONBOARDING-RUNBOOK.md (operator-facing): create invite (POST /api/v1/invites), send code over secure channel, coworker installs + redeems + chooses folders + runs preview + reviews sensitive panel + first sync; include the exact contributor scope set.

Add a revoke/rotate section: list tokens (GET /api/v1/tokens), revoke (DELETE /api/v1/tokens/:id), reissue via new invite; note that revoke is immediate because authenticate() rechecks the registry each request.
Update docs/LOCAL-GUI-APP.md and docs/OCEAN-TOOLBOX-BOOTSTRAP.md to reflect invite-exchange + preview + secret exclusion, removing 'paste raw token' language.
acceptance: scripts/ocean-install.sh runs on a clean machine (or documented manual steps) and ends at a runnable ocean:app without embedding any token.
docs/COWORKER-ONBOARDING-RUNBOOK.md walks operator from invite creation to verified first sync with the sensitive-file review step.
Revoke/rotate steps are documented and a revoked token is rejected on the next request.
docs no longer instruct coworkers to paste a raw token; GUI packaging decision (A vs B) is recorded with rationale.

phases.title: Security and launch review for coworker rollout
tasks: Run an end-to-end rehearsal: admin issues invite -> fresh device redeems -> chooses a real folder containing planted secrets -> preview shows sensitive panel -> first sync uploads only safe files under /coworkers/<name>/<device> -> delete attempt returns 403.

Confirm no invite code, raw token, or DATABASE_URL is present in committed code, manifests, ledger payloads, or docs; confirm bootstrap.json remains mode 0600.
Produce a go/no-go checklist and document remaining gaps (e.g., deferred Electron packaging, no OS background daemon) as blocked/future, not implied complete.

launchDefinitionOfDone: A coworker onboards with a one-time invite code (no raw token paste): admin issues invite, coworker redeems it in the GUI, and a scoped contributor token is stored at mode 0600.
Default secret-exclusion globs (.env, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials, .aws/.ssh, *.kdbx, *secret*) exclude credentials in CLI bootstrap, CLI ingest, and GUI, with no default bypass.
Dry-run/preview surfaces skipped files by reason and loudly flags sensitive matches before the first upload; GUI requires acknowledgement when sensitive files are found.
Contributor tokens are scoped (/coworkers/<name>, /sessions/<name>, /context/ocean-bedrock), capped at CONFIDENTIAL, and delete returns 403.
Token registry is backed by Postgres (longhouse.auth_tokens) behind unchanged src/auth.mjs signatures, with JSON->Postgres backfill verified idempotent, enabling multi-replica.
Operator runbook documents create-invite, install, redeem, review, first-sync, and revoke/rotate; revocation is rejected on the next request.
Security review passes end-to-end with zero raw secrets in any committed artifact, manifest, or ledger payload.
openDecisions: GUI packaging: ship documented 'npm run ocean:app' + installer script now (low effort, recommended) vs build Electron/Tauri double-click .app/.exe (higher effort) — spec defaults to documented run and defers the desktop build.

Invite redemption endpoint exposure: fully public POST /api/v1/invites/redeem vs requiring a low-privilege bootstrap token; single-use + short TTL + sha256-hashed code chosen as the mitigation either way.

Auth store cutover strategy: run Postgres and JSON in parallel (dual-read) during transition vs hard switch via OCEAN_AUTH_STORE — affects whether the bootstrap-admin env token must be re-seeded into Postgres.
Whether the explicit --include-secrets escape hatch should exist at all, or secret exclusion should be absolute (no override) for coworker-issued tokens.

This track is sequenced firingOrder=4 dependsOnWorkflows=[ocean-longhouse-router] as assigned; in practice the auth/invite/secret-exclusion/packaging work has NO hard dependency on the Longhouse data-plane router and could run in parallel — the only real coupling is that multi-mount routing would change where coworker files land. Flagged, but firingOrder kept as given.
Whether contributor scope should also include a per-coworker /handoffs or /vault-readonly prefix, or stay strictly to coworkers/sessions/context.
risks: Secret-exclusion globs are heuristic; a non-standard secret filename (e.g. a custom config holding API keys) can still sync. The preview/sensitive panel and contributor-only scope are the compensating controls, not a guarantee.

Postgres auth-store migration touches the authentication hot path (authenticate() runs per request). A regression or slow indexed lookup could lock everyone out or add latency; parity tests and an indexed hash lookup are required before cutover.
The bootstrap-admin token is currently seeded from env into tokens.json (src/server.mjs bootstrapAuth); the JSON->Postgres backfill must carry it or admin access is lost after cutover.
Invite endpoint is a new public-facing surface; without strict single-use + short TTL + rate limiting it becomes a token-minting vector. Must reject reuse/expired atomically.
Local app sync and scheduling only run while the GUI is open (no OS daemon); a coworker may believe sync is continuous. Runbook must state this explicitly.

Token registry hardening to Postgres assumes the same prod DATABASE_URL already used by ledger/sources; if Bedrock runs without DATABASE_URL the auth store must fall back to JSON cleanly or auth breaks.
Assigned dependency on ocean-longhouse-router is weak; if that wave slips, this track's auth/secret/packaging work is needlessly blocked unless the orchestrator allows it to proceed in parallel.
